entries.title: River home to 500 crocodiles chosen as Olympic rowing venue

entries.title: Michelin-starred Seoul restaurant fined for using ants as garnish

entries.title: U.N.-backed experts cite possible U.S. war crimes in Iran, including a school attack
entries.snippet: Human rights experts commissioned by the U.N. say they have found "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes in Iran, including a strike on a school in the southern city of Minab.

entries.title: The Fed raises interest rates. And, EU proposes Canada become an 'associate member'
entries.snippet: The Federal Reserve has raised interest rates for the first time in years. And, the European Union has proposed that Canada become its first-ever "associate member."

entries.title: Pressure on global chokepoints drives Asia's increased use of Arctic Trade Routes
entries.snippet: Asian nations began pilot voyages over a decade ago to find routes to Europe and the Middle East that were faster and less vulnerable to chokepoints. The ongoing war has added impetus to those efforts.

entries.title: Why reshaping memories may hold the key to raising self-esteem
entries.snippet: In a new book, psychologist Marisa Franco explains why it's good to feel good about yourself — and shares a helpful memory technique that we've turned into a printable worksheet.

entries.title: D.C. airspace is complicated. Experts say Trump's arch would add one more risk
entries.snippet: The Trump administration wants to build its 250-foot arch near one of the country's busiest runways. The FAA will determine whether that poses a hazard. But independent experts already have concerns.

entries.title: People's houses are collapsing into the ocean. FEMA gives them no other option
entries.snippet: Waterfront homes are collapsing along the coast. Homeowners generally have plenty of warning before their house buckles. So why aren't most houses removed, or at least emptied, before they fall?

entries.title: Pediatricians raise the alarm on the effect of Trump's immigration crackdown on kids
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has been pursuing a quiet immigration crackdown strategy: limiting access to health care and public services. The American Academy of Pediatrics is sounding the alarm about the impact on children.

entries.title: A Sikh truck driver is stabbed amid a rise in anti-South Asian rhetoric
entries.snippet: The driver said he was shaken by a violent encounter at a rest stop, which he described as unprovoked.

entries.snippet: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday embraced the prospect of his country becoming the European Union's first associate member, saying closer ties with the continent would ensure no country could control Canada's markets or undermine its sovereignty.

entries.title: EU chief Ursula von der Leyen proposes Canada becoming the bloc's 1st associate member
entries.snippet: Speaking in Charlotte, North Carolina, Trump suggested that allowing Canada to become an associate EU member could be a "hostile act" and threatened to respond to the proposed move by imposing more tariffs on the bloc.

entries.snippet: Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran and his bipartisan effort to force the release of more files in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation are all being left behind, blocked from votes.

entries.title: U.S. stocks slip after the Fed raises interest rates, hints more hikes may be on the way
entries.snippet: U.S. stocks slipped Wednesday after the Federal Reserve hiked its main interest rate for the first time in three years and suggested more may be ahead as it tries to get the nation's high inflation under control.

entries.title: The one issue where Republicans and Democrats are unified before the midterms, according to this poll
entries.snippet: Americans have grown more concerned about the environmental impacts of artificial intelligence over the last year, according to a new poll from The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research and the Energy Policy Institute at the University of Chicago.

entries.title: Trump administration has cut or frozen $177 billion in grants across every state, analysis shows
entries.snippet: Among the grants that were eliminated, frozen or delayed were ones related to maternal health in Michigan, education research in Mississippi and assistance to minority farmers in Iowa, the researchers found.

entries.title: Earth lost more than 12 trillion tons of ice from Greenland and Antarctica in 47 years, satellites show
entries.snippet: A major report has found that 12.5 trillion tons of ice from Greenland and Antarctica have melted since 1979. The massive glacier melt is mainly attributed to warmer waters eroding the ice sheets from below and the sides.

entries.title: Iran war has cost the U.S. more than $38 billion so far, budget office says
entries.snippet: The estimates come largely from replacing munitions and equipment lost in battle, the CBO said, and do not include costs related to U.S. military personnel killed or injured in the conflict or longer term effects.

entries.snippet: The House approved a resolution Wednesday holding billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress, referring the matter to the Department of Justice after he defied the Oversight Committee's subpoenas in its investigation into disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.

entries.title: Klopp wants Germany football team to 'reclaim the flag'
entries.snippet: Jürgen Klopp says he wants his Germany team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

entries.title: Serbia's President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
entries.snippet: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

entries.title: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
entries.snippet: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticisms of King Charles III in a new book from the brother of his late wife Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

entries.title: Canada's Carney welcomes associate status idea in EU speech
entries.snippet: Mark Carney wants to strengthen Canada's ties to the European Union amid a growing rift with the US under Donald Trump. The US president has threatened to halt trade with Europe if it makes Canada an associate EU member.

entries.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
entries.snippet: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

entries.title: Fiji declares HIV a national crisis, 1 in 60 adults carry it
entries.snippet: Fiji's government estimates that HIV prevalence has almost tripled in the last five years. It's expanding testing, prevention and treatment services. In 2025 the tiny island recorded 16 times more new cases than in 2019.

entries.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
entries.snippet: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

entries.title: Australia to restrict student, backpacker visas in migration clampdown
entries.snippet: The Australian interior minister said reducing migration is needed to address housing pressures. The move comes amid a far-right surge in the polls.

entries.title: Germany news: Mysterious explosions reported in Frankfurt
entries.snippet: A cafe and kiosk were damaged overnight in Frankfurt, in what police said are the latest in a series of mysterious blasts in the area. Meanwhile, diesel prices in Germany have hit an all-time high. More on DW.

entries.title: India news: New Delhi denies claims world leaders fell ill after BRICS summit
entries.snippet: India's foreign ministry rejected viral social media claims that leaders fell ill after the BRICS summit. Meanwhile, India defended its right to buy oil from diverse sources after the US passed a new sanctions bill.

entries.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
entries.snippet: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

entries.title: US extends visa denial for Palestinian officials ahead of UNGA
entries.snippet: The US State Department extended its visa sanctions on Palestinian officials, ahead of the UN General Assembly. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas will likely submit a video statement for the gathering.

entries.title: OpenAI discloses new 'concerning' behavior
entries.snippet: New transparency reports from OpenAI show that some AI models have engaged in deceptive behavior, raising fresh questions about the safety, reliability, and governance of advanced artificial intelligence.

entries.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes injure several in Kyiv, Odesa
entries.snippet: Russian airstrikes hit apartment buildings and warehouses in Ukraine, injuring several people, including a child.

entries.title: Trump threatens EU with further sanctions over Canada
entries.snippet: The EU had signaled that Canada is poised to become the bloc's first associate member. Trump called the idea both "laughable" and a "hostile act."

entries.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
entries.snippet: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

entries.title: US Congress passes Russia sanctions bill
entries.snippet: The sanctions package is considered the most substantial US legislative effort against Moscow since Trump returned to the White House. Measures in the bill could lead to secondary sanctions on India, China and Iran.

entries.title: Sweden's center-left bloc set to win election, STV reports
entries.snippet: The center-left opposition won the Swedish elections by a very slim margin, the public broadcaster reported after 99% of the votes were counted. Thorny negotiations await the bloc even if the result is confirmed.

entries.title: US Fed raises key rate for first time in 3 years
entries.snippet: In an attempt to address the persistently high inflation in the world's largest economy, the US Federal Reserve increased interest rates by 25 basis points. The president, on the other hand, said they should be cut.
